questions.q: Which phrase best summarizes TCM's guiding principle?
options: Adopt, not adapt
Customize everything to match legacy processes exactly
Design first, configure never
Test in production to save time
questions.explain: "Adopt, not adapt" means starting from Oracle's standard functionality and reference processes, extending only where a documented business need requires it.

questions.q: What role does the scribe play in a requirements workshop?
options: Approves the project budget
Performs the Oracle Fusion configuration
Signs off on the solution design document
Captures decisions and requirement IDs in real time
questions.explain: The scribe's job is to capture decisions and requirement IDs as the workshop happens, not after the fact.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a phase gate or milestone review?
options: To document bank account setup
A formal go/no-go checkpoint between TCM phases
A quarterly Oracle patch notification
A type of test script
questions.explain: Phase gates give the sponsor and project managers a formal decision point before moving into the next TCM phase, based on entry/exit criteria.

questions.q: Who typically serves as the Executive Sponsor on an Oracle Fusion Financials implementation?
options: A super user
A senior client leader, often the CFO
The Oracle Solution Architect
The Technical Consultant
questions.explain: The Executive Sponsor is a senior client leader, often the CFO on a Financials project, who owns the business case and resolves escalations.

questions.q: What does a Business Process Design (BPD) document primarily describe?
options: The technical build steps for an Oracle Integration Cloud process
The future-state business process end to end, in business terms, with who performs each step
The severity levels used for defect management
The bank account hierarchy only
questions.explain: A BPD narrates the future-state process end to end in business language, including process flow diagrams and the Oracle screen each step corresponds to.

questions.q: In a fit-gap session, what happens when a process owner confirms that standard Oracle functionality satisfies a requirement?
options: It is marked a Fit and moves to the configuration workbook
It is automatically escalated to an extension gap
It is removed from the Requirements Traceability Matrix
It requires a Service Request to Oracle Support
questions.explain: When standard functionality satisfies a requirement as-is, it is marked a Fit and moves directly to the configuration workbook.

questions.q: What is lost if a team configures Oracle Fusion directly from workshop notes, skipping a configuration workbook?
options: Nothing; the workbook is purely optional paperwork
The audit trail: why a setting was chosen, and a concrete item for business sign-off
The ability to run fit-gap analysis
The requirement's unique ID
questions.explain: Without a workbook, nobody can see why a setting was chosen, there's nothing concrete for business to sign off, and technical consultants lack a single source of truth.

questions.q: Which solution option involves the business changing how it works rather than changing the system?
options: Extension
Personalization
Process workaround
Configuration
questions.explain: A process workaround means the business adjusts its own process, with no change to the system itself.

questions.q: What did Brightfield's consultant check before importing the Cash Management configuration package into Test?
options: Nothing — packages are imported without review
The RAID log only
The comparison report, to confirm no one had manually changed settings directly in Test
The Executive Sponsor's calendar
questions.explain: The consultant reviewed FSM's comparison report against Test to catch any manual drift before importing the package.

questions.q: Why does scoping an Implementation Project tightly matter?
options: Because Oracle charges extra for unscoped task lists
Because scoping is required before fit-gap analysis can begin
Because unscoped projects cannot be opened
Because it keeps consultants focused on only the task lists relevant to their module, not Oracle's entire catalog
questions.explain: Oracle's full task catalog spans every module Oracle offers; scoping keeps a consultant focused on just what's relevant to their implementation.

questions.q: What is an update "cohort"?
options: A group of customers sharing the same quarterly update calendar
A group of defects with the same severity
A type of configuration package
A group of legal entities sharing one ledger
questions.explain: Customers are grouped into cohorts (commonly A, B, and C) tied to different months, so Oracle doesn't push updates to every customer simultaneously.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a mock conversion cycle?
options: To permanently load production data before go-live
To test Oracle Cloud Success Navigator
To replace the need for a configuration workbook
To run a practice data load well before cutover so problems are found on a non-critical timeline
questions.explain: Mock conversion cycles are practice loads run before the real cutover load, surfacing data problems early rather than during the actual cutover weekend.

questions.q: What does Oracle's update "readiness documentation" help a team decide?
options: Which Executive Sponsor to assign
What's changed in the update and which optional new features to opt into
How to write the original Business Requirements Document
The legal entity structure for Phase 2
questions.explain: Readiness documentation describes what's new or changed in an update, helping teams decide what to regression test and which opt-in features to enable.

questions.q: What does a formal UAT sign-off actually certify?
options: That the system has zero defects of any kind
That the Requirements Traceability Matrix is no longer needed
That hypercare has ended
That the system meets the business's acceptance criteria and is ready to run on, even with some minor defects open
questions.explain: UAT sign-off certifies the system is ready for the business to run on — not that it is defect-free, since lower-severity defects can remain open with an agreed plan.

questions.q: What should every test script trace back to?
options: A bank branch routing number
The Executive Sponsor's calendar
One or more requirement IDs in the Requirements Traceability Matrix
A Service Request severity level
questions.explain: Test scripts trace to requirement IDs in the RTM, closing the loop from requirement through configuration to proof that it works.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "steps to reproduce" on a defect log entry?
options: To document the Executive Sponsor's approval
To calculate the defect's priority automatically
So anyone, not just the original finder, can recreate the problem
To replace the need for a test script
questions.explain: Steps to reproduce let any team member recreate the defect, not just the person who originally found it.

questions.q: Why does something almost always surface during go-live even after thorough testing?
options: Because testing is pointless and should be skipped
Because real production volume and real user behavior inevitably include scenarios no script anticipated
Because Oracle intentionally breaks systems at go-live
Because the cutover plan is never actually followed
questions.explain: Even a well-tested go-live surfaces new edge cases from real users and real transaction volume — an expected reality, not evidence that testing failed.

questions.q: What is hypercare?
options: A type of Oracle Service Request
The intensive, stabilization-focused support period immediately following go-live
A phase of fit-gap analysis
A quarterly update readiness review
questions.explain: Hypercare is the elevated, intensive support period immediately after go-live, run by the implementation team itself.

questions.q: What happens at a go/no-go decision point during cutover?
options: The team decides whether to proceed to the next step or pause to fix a problem first
The project charter is signed
A new requirement is gathered
A configuration package is exported
questions.explain: Go/no-go decision points are checkpoints in the cutover runbook where the team decides whether to continue or pause based on validation results.

questions.q: What does Oracle's Severity 1 classification mean?
options: Production use is stopped or so severely impacted that work cannot reasonably continue
A minor inconvenience with an available workaround
A general question with no urgency
A cosmetic UI issue
questions.explain: Severity 1 means production is stopped or so severely impacted that the business cannot reasonably continue, triggering 24x7 response from Oracle.
